title: Unraveling the Immunogenicity of P.1 Variant of SARS-CoV-2 Emerged in Manaus, Amazonas: Insights from Molecular Dynamics and Machine-Learning Mutation Analysis
content: The emergence of the P.1 variant of the SARS-CoV-2 virus is primarily responsible for the serious 2nd wave of infections that occurred in the city of Manaus, Amazonas, Brazil in early 2021. However, few studies seek to understand at the molecular level the reason for this, in addition to how neutralizing antibodies of different classes were affected. It was compared the influence of P.1/Gamma variant on antibody-antigen interaction in addition to the consequences in affinity for human ACE2 receptor. Regarding the simulations where we compared the P.1 variant, in fact the latter induced greater structural instability in the ACE2-RBD interaction, which may translate into greater affinity. In this way, based on the computational results, we propose that there were other factors besides molecular factors that made P.1 responsible for the greatest public health crisis in Brazil, since the affinity of the antigen for the ACE2 receptor was higher. And therefore, the vaccination campaign was certainly decisive in the fight against the Covid-19 pandemic, as the virus has been adapting to the human species over time.
